tutor_message.content:
You are connecting the concept of BFS layers to group assignments quite nicely here. Remember though, the structure and properties of undirected graphs mean that the number of groups might depend on the longest possible shortest-path layering you can achieve from any node in a component—not just from the first node you start BFS with. This is because different BFS roots could reveal longer valid chains, changing the maximum m achievable for a component. 

It’s also important to keep in mind certain cycle structures (odd cycles, in particular) that might invalidate the grouping constraints. So, considering whether components are bipartite and evaluating the maximum layer count starting BFS from every node in a component might be necessary for correctness.
